the-order-of-combat:
Determine surprise, establish positions, roll initiative (Dexterity check; ties are settled among players and DM). A round lasts 6 seconds.
On your turn: Movement and one action, plus a bonus action if a feature grants one. One reaction per round, also outside your turn. One small object interaction is free, e.g. drawing a weapon.
Surprised: Can't move or act in the first round and can't react until that turn ends.
movement-and-position:
Splitting movement: Allowed, also before and after your action.
Difficult terrain: Every foot costs 1 extra foot.
Prone: Standing up costs half your speed, crawling costs 1 extra foot per foot. Attacks within 5 ft. have advantage, others disadvantage. Your own attacks have disadvantage.
Moving through enemies: Only if they are two sizes larger or smaller.
Space by size: Tiny 2.5 ft., Small and Medium 5 ft., Large 10 ft., Huge 15 ft., Gargantuan 20 ft. or more.
Squeezing: 1 extra foot per foot, disadvantage on attacks and Dexterity saves, attacks against you have advantage.
actions-in-combat:
Actions: Attack, Cast a Spell, Dash (double movement), Disengage (no opportunity attacks), Dodge (attacks against you have disadvantage, Dexterity saves advantage), Help (ally has advantage), Hide, Ready (set trigger and reaction; readied spells need concentration), Search, Use an Object.
Two-Weapon Fighting: Holding two light melee weapons, you can make a bonus action attack with the second after attacking, without adding your ability modifier to damage unless it is negative.
making-an-attack:
Roll: d20 + ability modifier + proficiency bonus against AC. A natural 20 always hits and is a critical (double the damage dice), a natural 1 always misses.
Unseen target: Disadvantage. Target can't see you: Advantage.
Ranged: Beyond normal range disadvantage, beyond long range impossible. Hostile creature within 5 ft.: Disadvantage.
Opportunity attack: Reaction, one melee attack when a visible enemy leaves your reach. Not against Disengage or teleportation.
Grapple and Shove: Instead of one attack; Strength (Athletics) against the target's Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics); target at most one size larger.
cover:
Half cover: +2 to AC and Dexterity saves.
Three-quarters cover: +5 to AC and Dexterity saves.
Total cover: Can't be targeted directly.
damage-and-healing:
Resistance halves, vulnerability doubles damage. Multiple instances of the same resistance count once.
At 0 HP: Unconscious and death saves (DC 10, three successes or three failures). Natural 20: 1 HP and conscious. Natural 1: two failures. Damage at 0 HP: one failure, a critical two.
Instant death: When the remaining damage equals or exceeds your HP maximum.
Stabilize: Medicine DC 10 as an action. A stable creature regains 1 HP after 1d4 hours.
Knocking out: When a melee hit drops a creature to 0 HP, the attacker can leave it unconscious and stable.
Temporary HP: Don't stack, the higher value counts.
advantage-and-disadvantage: Rule: Roll two d20, take the higher (advantage) or lower (disadvantage). Multiple sources don't stack. Having both cancels out, no matter how many sources.
ability-checks:
Typical DCs: Very easy 5, easy 10, medium 15, hard 20, very hard 25, nearly impossible 30.
Contest: Both roll, the higher result wins, a tie leaves the situation unchanged.
Group check: At least half must succeed.
movement:
Travel pace: Fast 4 miles per hour, 30 per day, −5 to passive Perception. Normal 3 and 24. Slow 2 and 18, stealth possible.
Forced march: From the ninth hour, Constitution save at the end of each hour, DC 10 + 1 per hour beyond 8, or 1 level of exhaustion.
Difficult terrain: Halves travel pace.
Jumping: Long jump with 10 ft. run-up as many feet as your Strength score, standing half. High jump with run-up 3 + Strength modifier feet, standing half.
Climbing and swimming: 1 extra foot per foot unless you have the matching speed.
the-environment:
Falling: 1d6 bludgeoning per 10 ft., at most 20d6, then prone.
Suffocating: Hold breath 1 + Constitution modifier minutes (at least 30 seconds). Then Constitution modifier rounds (at least 1), then 0 HP and dying.
Vision: Lightly obscured means disadvantage on sight-based Perception, heavily obscured means effectively blinded.
Darkvision: Dim light as bright light, darkness as dim light.
Food: 1 pound per day; without food 3 + Constitution modifier days (at least 1), then 1 level of exhaustion per day.
Water: 1 gallon per day, 2 in hot weather. With half: Constitution DC 15 or 1 level of exhaustion. With less: automatically 1 level.
resting:
Short rest: At least 1 hour. Spend hit dice, each heals the roll + Constitution modifier.
Long rest: At least 8 hours, at most 2 of them awake. Regain all HP and half your maximum hit dice (at least 1). Only one long rest per 24 hours, and you need at least 1 HP.
objects:
AC by material: Cloth, paper, rope 11; crystal, glass, ice 13; wood, bone 15; stone 17; iron, steel 19; mithral 21; adamantine 23.
HP (fragile / resilient): Tiny 1d4 / 2d4, Small 1d6 / 3d6, Medium 1d8 / 4d8, Large 1d10 / 5d10.
Immunities: Objects are immune to poison and psychic damage. The DM may ignore damage below a threshold.
traps:
Severity: Setback DC 10 to 11, attack +3 to +5. Dangerous DC 12 to 15, attack +6 to +8. Deadly DC 16 to 20, attack +9 to +12.
Damage by level (setback / dangerous / deadly): 1 to 4: 1d10 / 2d10 / 4d10. 5 to 10: 2d10 / 4d10 / 10d10. 11 to 16: 4d10 / 10d10 / 18d10. 17 to 20: 10d10 / 18d10 / 24d10.
